newsitem.title: UK: UK utility body proposes regulator advisory board.
newsitem.headline: UK utility body proposes regulator advisory board.

text.p: A British independent commission on regulation of privatised utilities on Tuesday reccomended advisory boards be set up for individual regulators and proposed that reasons for regulatory decisions should be published.

The Commission on the Regulation of Privatised Utilities said in its report that advisory boards would "reduce personalization of utility regulators and increase the transparency, effectiveness and legitimacy" of the regime.

It said that directors general of regulatory bodies should be required by statute to give reasons for their decisions and should publish an annual Application of Principles setting out the implications of their activities for their industries.

The report said that although directors general do publish reasons for their decisions, "there were complaints that insufficient reasons for decisions were given...there was a lack of clarity and transparency concerning the arguments and justification underlying."

The Commission rejected a single regulatory body to cover all utilities, an idea which has been suggested by some commentators, but said Oftel, which regulates the telecommunications industry, could be integrated with part of the Independent Television Commission.
It added that electricity regulator Offer and Ofgas, which watches over the gas industry, could be merged after full competition in the two areas is established in 1998.

The Commission, which is backed by education charity the Hansard Society and independent think-tank the European Policy Forum, started its review in October 1995 and considered regulation in electricity, water, telecommunications and gas.
It is independent and not affiliated to any political party and there is no obligation for its recommendations to be followed by parliament.
The Commission's report called on the government to publish an "explicit framework" for utilities to meet "social objectives such as universal service or energy conservation."
The Commission said that competition policy should be strengthened with enforcement by the industry regulators with the role of the Secretary of State in takeovers and mergers diminishing.
The Commission is chaired by John Flemming, warden of Wadham College at Oxford University and a former chief economist at the Bank of England.
It meets around once a month and receives written evidence from around 70 bodies including the regulators themselves.
